name: Matrimony.com Ltd
tagline: Cheap (EV ex-cash ~Rs 500 Cr) category monopoly with ~100% of industry profits; operating leverage now confirmed for two straight quarters (Q4 FY26 + Q1 FY27 PAT +127% YoY, EBITDA margin 11% -> 20%) with management guiding a third; promoter stake rising, 3rd buyback done - re-rating setup, partly de-risked
business_overview: Matrimony.com runs India's largest online matchmaking franchise (BharatMatrimony and community-specific portals), estimated at ~50% of industry revenue and close to (or above) 100% of industry profits. It also incubates allied businesses - Luv.com (alternate matchmaking), Mandap.com and wedding services, and ManyJobs (an early-stage jobs platform) - most of which are small and loss-making. The core matchmaking platform has grown paid subscribers and billings at high-single-digit rates over a decade; recent growth has been ATV-led (Elite Matrimony, personalised services) with a shift toward annual (from quarterly) subscription packages.
fundamentals_table: ~Rs 1,078 Cr (price ~Rs 521); EV ex-cash ~Rs 500 Cr (net cash >Rs 300 Cr)
~24x trailing; ~13-14x on an FY27 PAT of ~Rs 80 Cr+; EV ex-cash ~6-7x forward PAT
5-yr sales CAGR ~4% (poor); Q1 FY27: billings +7.8% YoY, matchmaking revenue +13.6% YoY, PAT +127.5% YoY (Rs 19.1 Cr); paid subs +3.7% YoY / +15.9% QoQ
Enterprise EBITDA margin 20.1% in Q1 FY27 vs 11.0% Q1 FY26 and 12.4% Q4 FY26; FY26 PAT Rs 34 Cr (aided by ~Rs 23.9 Cr other income); guided run-rate PAT ~Rs 80 Cr+
3rd buyback in 4 years completed (8,93,129 shares extinguished); promoter holding ~58.4% and rising (non-tendering + open-market buys); dividend payout ~30%, yield ~1%
fundamentals_narrative: On a trailing 5-year view this looks like a no-growth business (sales CAGR ~4%, OPM halved). The recent-quarter picture is different: billings and revenue are growing again, marketing intensity from the main competitor (Info Edge's Jeevansathi) is easing, and with a largely fixed cost base the operating leverage is showing up as PAT more than doubling YoY. The company is net cash (>Rs 300 Cr), buying back stock for a third time in four years, and the promoter is adding shares in the open market - so per-share economics compound even without much topline. Offsetting risk: paid-subscriber counts are structurally flat-to-down (successful marriages churn users out), and management has started allocating capital to startup investing.
technical_read: Not independently pulled. Stock ranged ~Rs 363-574 over 52 weeks; multiple thread posts describe it as 'written off' / 'left for dead' by the market, with billings growth and Q2 FY27 results as the catalysts for a potential re-rating.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 72 posts, Feb 2024 to Aug 2026. The thread has crystallised into a well-argued 'why now' bull case over 2026: (1) valuation - minus cash the business trades at an EV of ~Rs 500 Cr on ~Rs 35 Cr+ industry-wide net profit that Matrimony largely owns; (2) capital returns - three buybacks in four years plus a non-tendering, open-market-buying promoter imply a mid-teens buyback+dividend yield; (3) competition easing - Info Edge under investor pressure to stop funding Jeevansathi's losses; (4) operating leverage - the FY26 shift to ~10% annual subscriptions understated subscriber optics but added deferred revenue, and Q1/Q2 FY27 show 'high operating leverage kicked in' with PAT more than doubling and guidance for full-year PAT of ~Rs 80 Cr+ (a record); (5) management pushing growth via new business heads for assisted matrimony, ManyJobs, Mandap and wedding services, plus a Havas Media partnership for AI-driven regional marketing. The persistent bear case, made by thoughtful posters: paid profiles do not sustainably grow because the product 'works' and users leave; ATV-led growth eventually saturates; ad spend has not come down much in absolute terms; and a new startup-investing allocation is an unquantified capital-allocation risk. Manivannan (10 loves) presented a formal 'owner-operated, structurally advantaged platform' thesis at an investing summit.

valuepickr_forum.consensus_view: Cheap monopoly; operating leverage inflection now underway

bse_notes: Three buybacks in four years; the promoter has consistently NOT tendered, raising his stake, and additionally bought ~2.89 lakh shares (~1.3% of equity) in the open market Sep-Nov 2025 and ~3.5% more in a subsequent quarter (>Rs 30 Cr). Nalanda and MIT (institutional holders) reduced via buyback tenders. New board appointment to support a startup-investing initiative (2025) - flagged in-thread as a capital-allocation watch item. Net cash >Rs 300 Cr.
bull_case: Dominant category leader (~50% of revenue, ~100% of industry profits) trading at an EV ex-cash of only ~Rs 500 Cr - a 'melting ice cube' price for a franchise that keeps making money through hyper-competition
Competitive intensity easing as Info Edge faces pressure to stop funding Jeevansathi's losses - the swing factor for marketing spend and margins
High operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base: Q1/Q2 FY27 PAT more than doubling YoY; guided full-year PAT ~Rs 80 Cr+ (record)
Aggressive shareholder returns - 3rd buyback in 4 years plus a non-tendering, open-market-buying promoter -> mid-teens buyback+dividend yield and rising per-share ownership
Optionality from ManyJobs, wedding services, Elite/Jodi segmentation and a Havas Media regional-marketing partnership; net cash >Rs 300 Cr
bear_case: Structural: paid-subscriber counts are flat-to-declining because a successful match removes the customer - growth has to be re-won every quarter plus more
Recent growth is ATV/price-led (Elite, personalised services), which can saturate; trailing 5-year sales CAGR is only ~4% and OPM has halved to ~10%
Advertising spend has not fallen meaningfully in absolute terms yet - the operating-leverage thesis depends on that changing and holding for several quarters
New startup-investing capital allocation is an unquantified risk on a cash-generative balance sheet with no clear stated policy
10x on ~Rs 1,067 Cr needs PAT toward ~Rs 250 Cr+ and a re-rating to ~40x - aggressive for a business the market has repeatedly refused to re-rate
verdict_headline: Deep-value category monopoly with the operating-leverage inflection now confirmed for two straight quarters and guided for a third - partly de-risked since last pass, but a true 10x still needs a re-rating the market has refused for a decade
verdict_reasoning: Per the recent-inflection rule, the weak 5-yr average is overridden by a confirmed near-term change: Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 both delivered ~+127% YoY PAT with enterprise EBITDA margin moving 11% -> 20%, and management explicitly guides Q2 FY27 to another triple-digit PAT gain plus double-digit billing/revenue growth

With a dominant moat (~50% of industry revenue, ~100% of profits), EV ex-cash of only ~Rs 500 Cr on a guided ~Rs 80 Cr+ FY27 PAT, a rising promoter stake and a 3rd completed buyback, the 10x-in-2-3-years frame is defensible - four_box = 3.0

Conviction held at Medium (not raised): the 10x rests on multiple expansion the market has repeatedly declined to grant, topline is still only ~+8% billings, FY26 earnings leaned on ~Rs 23.9 Cr other income, paid-subscriber stagnation is structural, and the startup-investing allocation is an unquantified capital-allocation question
Re-check trigger: Q3/Q4 FY27 sustaining 18-20%+ EBITDA margin with a visible absolute decline in ad spend, plus a stated policy on the startup-investing allocation

four_box.note: tailwind weak (no secular demand growth - successful matches churn users out; the lift is cyclical operating leverage + easing competition, not a structural driver). tam yes (category leader with room in ATV, wedding services, jobs). moat yes (~50% of industry revenue, ~100% of profits, community-portal network effects). valuation weak (24x trailing is not cheap on optics, but EV ex-cash ~Rs 500 Cr on a guided ~Rs 80 Cr+ FY27 PAT is - thesis not priced in). Score 3.0 -> 10x-in-2-3-years permitted; conviction held Medium because the label depends on multiple expansion the market has declined for years.

How much capital goes into the startup-investing allocation, and under what policy?
How durable is the paid-subscriber uptick given the 'product works, users leave' structural dynamic?
deep_dive.conviction_update: Medium -> Medium. The operating-leverage thesis is materially de-risked since last pass (two confirmed quarters + explicit Q2 guidance, promoter buying, buyback done, EV ex-cash ~Rs 500 Cr on ~Rs 80 Cr+ guided PAT), but a true 10x still needs a re-rating the market has refused for a decade and topline growth is only ~+8%, so conviction holds rather than rises.

track_record.note: Over FY22-FY26, only one year plausibly cleared BOTH revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% - the 5-yr revenue CAGR is ~4% and OPM was compressed by the ad-spend war for most of the window. ROCE mostly sat in the mid-teens. This is a monopoly with a poor growth record, now inflecting; the consistency score should be low.
